said: Explain how a heat pump works, in detail.
told: A heat pump uses the vapor-compression refrigeration cycle to move heat from a cooler source, such as outdoor air, ground or water, to a warmer sink like your home. The refrigerant absorbs heat in the evaporator and becomes low-pressure gas, is compressed by an electric compressor so its pressure and temperature rise, then releases heat in the condenser and condenses into liquid. An expansion valve abruptly drops its pressure and temperature below outdoor conditions, so it can absorb more heat a ...
reply: It's a refrigerator backwards: the refrigerant sucks heat out of air, ground or water, gets compressed so its temperature climbs, dumps that heat into your home, then drops pressure and starts again. You get more heat than the electricity you put in, because most of it was already sitting outside. Nice trick for a machine with no fuel to burn, though not exactly free.
note: Correct and grounded in facts, not particularly flavourful but not bad either.
